Notifications show that the server runs and warn when it has trouble. Nearby devices lets tablets and plotters on the boat\'s network reach it; without it only this phone can. An unrestricted battery keeps Android from stopping it overnight.

The phone\'s battery, barometer, GPS, attitude, rate of turn, compass and cabin sensors reach Signal K through the Pocket SK Android bridge plugin. Turn each on or off, set its period and the bow offset in the plugin\'s settings in the admin UI.

With the phone in its holder and the boat lying level and still, tap Level now: roll and pitch then read zero as the phone sits. Until then the phone is taken to lie flat, screen up, with its top towards the bow.

The phone\'s GPS is not reaching Signal K: the server was started without the app on the screen (at boot or from the tile), and Android then gives it no location. Starting it again from here brings the GPS in.

GPS and AIS receivers and NMEA 0183 interfaces, plugged in by USB or paired over Bluetooth, reach Signal K through the Android bridge plugin, each as the source android.<device>. Set each USB device\'s baud rate in the plugin\'s settings in the admin UI; 4800 unless set.

Where the server keeps its .signalk folder: charts, server state, application data, logs, each plugin\'s data, and copies of its settings, its passwords and the plugins\' settings. On the phone or on a card it is the app\'s own folder, which goes with the app when it is uninstalled. The plugins themselves stay in the app\'s private storage, where Android lets them run.
No SD card or USB drive is in the phone.

From a computer over USB: Android/data/fi.pocketsk/files/signalk, on the phone or on the card, is the server\'s .signalk, as on a Linux box. Charts and other data copied there are the server\'s at once; a settings file changed, added or deleted there goes into the server when it next starts. Anyone who can open the folder can read security.json.
The server restarts and copies its data to %1$s first; with many charts that takes minutes. From then on it waits for the card whenever the card is out.
The server restarts and copies its data to the phone first. A folder whose card is not in the phone starts again empty; its data stays on the card.
From a browser: the server\'s Pocket SK files page, among its webapps, uploads charts and other files into its data, wherever it is.
From a computer over USB: copy them into the phone\'s Android/data/fi.pocketsk/files/inbox/charts (or inbox/<folder>). They are taken in when the server starts, or now with Take them in.
No webapps installed. Freeboard-SK, KIP and others are in the admin UI\'s App Store.

The Signal K server's .signalk folder (Pocket SK)

This is the server's configuration folder, as /home/node/.signalk is on a Linux box.

The folders here (charts, serverstate, applicationData, logs, and each plugin's data in plugin-config-data) are the server's own: what you copy in, the server sees at once.

The files directly here and in plugin-config-data (settings.json, security.json, the SSL key and certificate, the plugins' settings) are copies of the server's, brought up to date every 30 seconds while it runs. A copy you change, add or delete goes into the server when it next starts: stop and start it in Pocket SK, or restart it from the admin UI. Until then the server's own changes to that file do not overwrite yours. Deleting security.json and restarting the server resets its users and passwords, as on a Linux box.

node_modules, the installed plugins and webapps, is not here: Android runs code only from the app's private storage. Install and remove them in the admin UI's App Store.

security.json holds the server's users and the key its logins are signed with: anyone who can open this folder can read it.
